moveDecisions.rationale: The move directly presents a central affirmative causal route, but it does not itself complete the motion-level identification of the proposed source with God.

The necessary-being claim materially advances the central Thomistic foundation, while its universal scope and required qualification remain compressed; its core contingency terminology is nevertheless stable.
This is a clear constructive presentation of the intelligent-order bridge, directly connecting natural regularity to the proposed directing mind without yet completing the whole motion.
The move clearly advances the affirmative moral-ground route, and its principal terms and scope remain stable even though the crucial uniqueness qualification is not supplied.

The move supplies motion-level burden analysis rather than answering the affirmative arguments' internal premises, and it substantively represents the live theistic position while challenging its definition and falsifiability.

The stated evidential and revisable nonbelief applies generally to the affirmative case without contacting its individual inferential components, while directly supporting the negative motion-level burden.

The hiddenness argument bears more closely on the claimed directing deity than on the moral-law inference, supports the negative hiddenness bridge, and explicitly limits its scope to relevant God concepts.

The move offers relevant contrary material about reported divine communication without contacting the natural-regularity inference itself, and it positively supports the negative revelation and hiddenness bridge.

The move is important but largely repeats the burden dispute; it challenges exclusive affirmative burden while failing to answer the explicit distinction between tentative nonbelief and positive contrary assertion.

The move diagnoses the extrapolation problem and states its defeating consequence for the causal and contingency routes, but its separate assertion that existence is necessarily temporal exceeds the supplied warrant.

The move explicitly diagnoses why an unspecified first cause does not establish God or a directing mind, directly attacks the motion-level identification, and acknowledges the limits of its conclusion.

This is a central methodological challenge that explicitly defeats admission of an undemonstrated candidate; the magic analogy weakens the opposing account somewhat, and a limiting caveat remains implicit.

The move explicitly connects acknowledged ignorance to the causal, necessary-being, and reciprocal-burden claims, while centrally supporting the negative methodological-restraint route against supernatural gap filling.

The methodological defense is a major exchange, but it only partially answers the candidate-admission objection and does not identify independent positive evidence beyond labeling the inference inductive.

The conditional account coherently supplies an accountable secular alternative to divine grounding, centrally advances the negative morality route, clearly states its adopted standard, and expressly concedes that the standard need not be accepted.

The move constructively answers the stated evil question through privation and proposed greater goods, remains a subsidiary affirmative defense, and does not materially represent a developed opposing alternative.

The move clearly develops the central secular-morality bridge and distinguishes agreed standards from objective assessment, but its categorical claim that God solves no secular moral problem is materially stronger than demonstrated.

The move attacks the negative burden position but does not contact the explicitly tentative, revisable nonbelief actually stated; it also materially conflates atheism with broader metaphysical naturalism.

The move challenges morality relative to adopted well-being standards but leaves unanswered whether divine grounding avoids equivalent arbitrariness, so it only partially answers the compound negative case.

The interpersonal analogy partially answers the demand for public demonstration but supplies no criterion for false divine messages and does not justify a full reframe of the negative evidential challenge.
